title: Mittag-Leffler submodule in a universally exact sequence
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be a universally exact short exact sequence of $R$-modules, meaning that tensoring this sequence over $R$ with every $R$-module remains exact. If $M_2$ is a Mittag-Leffler $R$-module [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module], then $M_1$ is a Mittag-Leffler $R$-module.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary family $(Q_{\alpha})_{\alpha\in A}$ of $R$-modules. Tensoring the universally exact sequence with $\prod_{\alpha}Q_{\alpha}$ gives an exact top row $0	o M_1\otimes_R\prod_{\alpha}Q_{\alpha}	o M_2\otimes_R\prod_{\alpha}Q_{\alpha}	o M_3\otimes_R\prod_{\alpha}Q_{\alpha}	o0$. Tensoring it separately with each $Q_{\alpha}$ and taking the componentwise product gives an exact bottom row $0	o\prod_{\alpha}(M_1\otimes_RQ_{\alpha})	o\prod_{\alpha}(M_2\otimes_RQ_{\alpha})	o\prod_{\alpha}(M_3\otimes_RQ_{\alpha})	o0$. The canonical tensor-to-product maps form a commutative diagram between these rows, by their definition on pure tensors and linearity.

source.place: Tag 059N, lemma-pure-submodule-ML, proof: the displayed commutative diagram and the assertion that both rows are exact.

proof.text: The middle vertical map in this diagram is injective because $M_2$ is Mittag-Leffler, whose defining condition [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module] asserts injectivity of the canonical map for every family of modules. If an element of $M_1\otimes_R\prod_{\alpha}Q_{\alpha}$ maps to zero in $\prod_{\alpha}(M_1\otimes_RQ_{\alpha})$, commutativity sends its image in $M_2\otimes_R\prod_{\alpha}Q_{\alpha}$ to zero in the product of the $M_2$ tensors; injectivity of the middle vertical map makes that image zero. The top row is exact at $M_1\otimes_R\prod_{\alpha}Q_{\alpha}$, so its first arrow is injective and the original element is zero. Thus the canonical map for this arbitrary family is injective, and $M_1$ is Mittag-Leffler by the same definition.
